stem.text: A function g satisfies \( \lim_{x \to -6^{-}} g(x) = -\infty \). Describe in words what this statement says about g and about its graph.

answer_key.label: As x approaches \( -6 \) from the left, g(x) decreases without bound, so the line \( x = -6 \) is a vertical asymptote.

worked_solution.text: The input approaches \( -6 \) from the left only, and the output is not approaching any number.
worked_solution.rule_named: read the input side and the output behaviour

worked_solution.text: The values g(x) decreases without bound, which is what an infinite limit means, so the graph has the vertical asymptote \( x = -6 \).

options.label: As x approaches \( -6 \) from either side, g(x) decreases without bound, so the line \( x = -6 \) is a vertical asymptote.
options.derivation: the one sided statement read as describing the behaviour on both sides of the input

options.label: As x approaches \( -6 \) from the left, the limit of g(x) exists and equals \( -\infty \), so there is no asymptote at \( x = -6 \).
options.derivation: the statement that the limit equals infinity read as a statement that the limit exists
